title: Red light plus green light makes…?
hook: A screen pixel is three tiny lights. Turn two of them up and guess the colour.

knows: that three numbers describe a pixel's colour
doesNotKnow: that screens add light, so red plus green looks yellow

misconception: Colours on a screen mix like paint, so red plus green gives brown.
objective: The learner can explain that rgb(255, 255, 0) is yellow because a pixel's three lights add, and that raising blue moves it toward white, the opposite of mixing paint.

claims.text: A pixel set to red 255, green 255, blue 0 looks yellow.
claims.source: CSS Color Module Level 4, named colours: yellow = #ffff00 = rgb(255, 255, 0). The stage paints the swatch with exactly that value. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): CSS yellow = #ffff00.

claims.text: With all three lights at 255 the pixel is white; with all at 0 it is black.
claims.source: CSS Color Module Level 4: white = #ffffff, black = #000000. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.
8 bits per channel in sRGB colour as used by CSS rgb() (CSS Color Module Level 4, 'The RGB functions'). 255 = 2^8 - 1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: The stage names the eight corner colours black, red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta and white; CSS calls rgb(0,255,0) lime, rgb(0,255,255) aqua and rgb(255,0,255) fuchsia.
claims.source: CSS Color Module Level 4 named colours (lime #00ff00, aqua/cyan #00ffff, fuchsia/magenta #ff00ff). 'green' and 'magenta' here are everyday names, disclosed. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): CSS Color 4: lime #00ff00, aqua = cyan #00ffff, fuchsia = magenta #ff00ff; CSS green is #008000, so the disclosure is needed and present.

claims.text: A screen pixel gives off light and its three lights add, so adding light only makes it brighter.
claims.source: Additive colour mixing: Hunt, The Reproduction of Colour, 6th ed., ch. 2 (additive and subtractive mixing); emissive displays combine red, green and blue primaries additively. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Additive mixing of emitted light; correct. Hunt chapter number not confirmed, but the claim is standard colour science.

claims.text: Each pigment soaks up some light, so mixing paints leaves less light, which is why red and green paint make a dark brown.
claims.source: Subtractive mixing: Hunt, The Reproduction of Colour, ch. 2. 'Dark brown' is the typical result for red and green artists' paints, not an exact colour; stated narrowly. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): 'Dark brown' for red + green paint is the usual outcome and the claim is hedged; no exact colour is stated.

claims.text: Raising blue on a yellow pixel makes it paler, and at blue 255 it is white.
claims.source: rgb(255,255,128) and rgb(255,255,255) as painted by the stage; white per c2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): The stage paints rgb(255,255,128) then white; paler is accurate.

recall.question: A pixel shows red 255, green 0, blue 255. Is it darker or lighter than the pure red pixel (255, 0, 0)?
recall.why: A screen adds light, so turning blue on adds to the red; it never takes light away the way paint does.
